status_summary: FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research has continued a voluntary Quality Management Maturity prototype assessment program, with notices on 2025-04-23 and 2026-02-11 opening second and third years for up to nine volunteer establishments that receive scored reports; the notices do not say scores are published. An FDA program page current as of 2026-07-01 says in its description that FDA has proposed the development of a rating system, an intention with no stated timetable and no statement that ratings would be public or replace pass/fail inspection outcomes. Executive Order 14293 of 2025-05-05 directed FDA to consider publicly listing noncompliant facilities and to disclose foreign inspection counts by country and manufacturer, which is related to but not the same as facility codes on packaging or a graded inspection system. An FDA notice of 2025-08-08 on onshoring drug manufacturing (public meeting held 2025-09-30) mentions quality management maturity only as content of a proposed PreCheck application, and no step on exempting generics from rebates or on NIH or FDA new-use trials was found.

timeline.event: FDA published a notice opening a second year of the voluntary Quality Management Maturity prototype assessment program (up to nine establishments, scored reports to participants).

Executive Order 14293, Regulatory Relief To Promote Domestic Production of Critical Medicines (published 2025-05-08), directed FDA to improve enforcement of drug establishment data reporting, including considering public display of a list of noncompliant facilities, and to disclose annual foreign inspection counts by country and manufacturer.

FDA published a notice of a public meeting (held 2025-09-30) and request for comments on onshoring manufacturing of drugs and biological products, mentioning quality management maturity within proposed PreCheck application content.
FDA published a notice opening a third year of the voluntary Quality Management Maturity program, accepting requests through 2026-04-13.

title: Cut drug shortages: graded facility ratings, facility codes, rebate exemption, trials
uncertainties: Executive Order 14293 and the onshoring public meeting notice (federalregister.gov) and the CDER Quality Management Maturity presentation of 2026-04-22 (fda.gov) were read by the researcher and again in review on 2026-10-18; none adopts graded inspection ratings in place of pass/fail outcomes, facility codes on packaging or a searchable product-facility database. The program is voluntary per its Federal Register notices and predates 2025-01-20; the presentation shows anonymized scores, links quality problems to shortages and does not say ratings will be published. On 2026-10-22 the FDA program page (fda.gov, current as of 2026-07-01) was read; the statement that FDA has proposed the development of a rating system appears in the page description rather than the body text, which says CDER is establishing a program to promote quality management maturity; no timetable is given and nothing says ratings will be published or replace pass/fail outcomes, so it is treated as an intention that fits the proposed stage, not as an operative step. The 2025-04-23 notice could not be re-opened on federalregister.gov on 2026-10-22 and was read instead on a third-party copy hosted by justia.com (90 FR 17069 to 17071, requests through 2025-06-09, scored reports to participants only), which matches the record; the third-party copy keeps confidence within medium. Federal Register API searches for drug shortage since 2025-01-20 returned 15 documents (including CMS pricing models and a Medicare proposed rule on made in America essential medicines of 2026-01-29) and none on generic rebate exemptions; the GLOBE and GUARD models and the 2026-01-29 CMS proposed rule were not read. An external retrieval of 2026-10-22 searched FDA, Federal Register and Congress.gov sources for facility identifiers on drug packaging and for a generic drug exemption from Medicaid rebate requirements and found no FDA proposal, guidance or bill on either; absence in those searches does not rule out an action, and Medicaid rebates are mainly a CMS and statutory matter. Not checked: whether FDA has published the section 3 list of noncompliant facilities, the August 2025 order on the strategic API reserve, NIH or FDA new-use trial announcements, and a RAPS and trade-press account of an FDA rating-system proposal that was surfaced earlier but not opened.
